main_text.p: ergo fieri potuit, vt Paulus, & Eugenius, qui restitutioni Photij praefederunt, a Ioan-ne Nono mitterentur. Quod si restitutioni Photij calculum dederunt, necessario a Io-anne Octavo, non a Nono legati sunt: Et ne dicas hunc errorem, vel calami nimium festinantis, vel Typographi cura expertis in-repsisse, ipse firmat Interpres, qui infra cum de eodem Ioanne sermo recideret, Photij restitutionem sub Ioanne Nono contigisse ingeminat; Primam sub Nicolao, qua Ignatium depofuit, & Tertiam sub Ioanne Nono, qua Photium restituit. Sequitur; legationibus functi cum praesidendi ritu inter Episcopos. Et tamen praesidendi ritus in ea Synodo, quidquid Interpres somniet, inversus est, & Praesidentiam Legatis Pontificijs in Synodo debitam Photius vsurpavit, & Thronum primum insedit. Hoc-q; non nisi cæcus, & Græcæ linguæ plane ignarus negaverit; cum sæpius atque iterate in ea inculcetur; [illegible, ~12 letters] τῷ Φωτίῳ. Et non solum Photium muneri suo redonatum. Ex cerebro loquitur, & quæ vellet ita fuisse, de facili ita facta esse pronunciat. Photius in ea Synodo ante consensum Locumtenentium Papæ a Schismaticis, excommunicatis, & Imperatoria potestate in locum, unde ceciderat, reponitur: imo numquam eum de gradu suo ce-

page.notes: The Greek phrase in the sixth line is only partly legible; the visible letters suggest the anathema formula ending in τῷ Φωτίῳ, but I could not read it letter by letter, so the opening is marked illegible. The sentence "Hocq; non nisi" is hyphenated across a line end as printed ("Hoc-q;"), and I kept that hyphen. The catchword "ce-" is the start of the next page. There are no margin notes, headings or running head on this page. Small marks at the bottom of the scan are a printer's or binder's smudge and are not text.
